# Contributors

Islam.wiki is a community-maintained knowledge base. This page explains how to contribute new content, corrections, and translations.

## Content types you can contribute

- Corrections to existing Hadith text or grading
- Missing translations for existing content
- New article drafts on Islamic topics
- Biographical information for scholars not yet in the database
- Corrections to isnad chains or narrator information
- Translation improvements

## How to submit a correction

1. Visit the page you want to correct on [islam.wiki](https://islam.wiki)
2. Click the "Suggest edit" button (requires a free account)
3. Make your change and add a brief explanation with your source
4. Submit — a moderator will review and approve

For corrections with scholarly sources, include the source in the edit note (e.g., "Grading per al-Albani in Silsilah al-Sahihah, no. 123").

## Trust levels

New accounts start at Trust Level 0 — all edits go to a review queue. After a few approved edits, accounts are promoted to Trust Level 1 and minor edits are auto-approved.

| Level | Name | Editing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | New | All edits pending review |
| 1 | Trusted | Minor edits auto-approved |
| 2 | Editor | Most edits auto-approved; can review Level 0/1 edits |
| 3 | Moderator | All edits auto-approved; can review and ban |

## Content standards

All content follows Ahl us-Sunnah wal-Jamaah methodology. See [[Theological-Guidelines]] for the full standards.

Key rules:
- Primary sources (Quran, Hadith) take precedence over secondary sources
- Grading must cite a specific scholar and source, not general consensus
- Articles should be neutral and descriptive, not polemical
- Unverified claims should be clearly marked as such

## Adding a new scholar biography

If you want to add a scholar not yet in the database:

1. Check that they are not already listed under a different name spelling
2. Create a new entry via the "Add scholar" form on the People section
3. Required fields: full name (Arabic), full name (transliterated), generation (Sahabi/Tabi/Tabi' al-Tabi'in), death date (Hijri)
4. Recommended: birth year, key teachers, key students, major works, brief bio
